judgment.reason: The query follows from premises p22 and p3 via valid first-order logic. (1) Take any person x. (2) From p22: there exists a person y₀ such that x admires y₀. (3) From p3: if x admires y₀, then y₀ helps x. (4) By modus ponens: y₀ helps x. (5) By existential generalization: there exists a person y such that y helps x. (6) Since x was arbitrary, universal generalization yields: for every person x, there is a person y such that y helps x. The color-entry recording premises (p0, p1, etc.) are logically irrelevant to the query and do not affect the derivation.
